summary: 34-year-old nurse with previous anaphylaxis to latex gloves listed for laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Pre-operative assessment for planned gallbladder operation
inputs.hpi: Symptomatic gallstones, listed for laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Anaphylaxis (wheeze, facial swelling, hypotension) when examined with latex gloves at a dental appointment in 2019; carries an adrenaline auto-injector. Also itching with bananas and avocado. Last menstrual period 12 days ago.

exam.general: Well. HR 72, BP 118/74, RR 14, SpO2 99% on air, T 36.7°C. BMI 24.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Multiple mobile gallstones, gallbladder wall 2 mm, no pericholecystic fluid. CBD 4 mm. Liver normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Pre-operative assessment — symptomatic gallstones; latex anaphylaxis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Symptomatic cholelithiasis. Latex anaphylaxis 2019 — latex-free theatre pathway.

mustInclude.note: Known latex anaphylaxis: latex-free theatre, ward and equipment.

mustInclude.proposedFix: Add an anaesthetic-alert rule set (PMH/allergy text: malignant hyperthermia, suxamethonium apnoea/butyrylcholinesterase, latex, difficult airway, OSA) that raises a persistent red flag and a plan line (trigger-free anaesthesia + dantrolene; avoid suxamethonium/mivacurium; latex-free theatre, first on list).

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: RCoA NAP6 — Perioperative anaphylaxis
guideline.section: Antibiotics (teicoplanin, co-amoxiclav) are the commonest triggers; allergy history must be checked before induction; latex remains a cause and requires a latex-free pathway in known allergy
guideline.citation: Royal College of Anaesthetists. Anaesthesia, surgery and life-threatening allergic reactions: 6th National Audit Project. London: RCoA; 2018.

guideline.name: AAGBI safety guideline — suspected anaphylactic reactions associated with anaesthesia
guideline.section: Patients with known latex allergy: latex-free environment and equipment, ideally first on the operating list
guideline.citation: Association of Anaesthetists of Great Britain and Ireland. Suspected anaphylactic reactions associated with anaesthesia. Anaesthesia. 2009;64:199–211.

rationale: Permutation: a non-drug allergy that changes theatre set-up. Tests the allergy alert and whether any output adds a latex-free pathway.
